The R sounds

The rule

My tailor is rich.Rich has a real /r/. Tailor has none at all: it ends /ˈteɪlə/,see lesson on schwa.

The /r/ sound is one of the hardest sounds in English, and notes that it is one of the last sounds English children master. It is not the French r. The French r is made in the throat. The English one is not.

  1. Your lips form a slight o shape.
  2. Your tongue curls up at the sides.
  3. You tighten the pharynx.

In British English a written r is often not pronounced at all. Instead it stretches the vowel in front of it.

cat /æ/  →  cart /ɑː/   ·   car /ɑː/
The r did not disappear. It turned into length.

Two places this happens: before a consonant (cart, port, hard, network) and at the end of a word (car, power, server).

1 · The two words that prove it

SERVER

Two written r's. Neither one is pronounced.

/ˈsɜːvə/   The first r stretches the vowel. The second is a schwa.

CIRCUIT

The word you say more than any other in this department.

/ˈsɜːkɪt/   The r you have been sounding all year is silent. It only makes the vowel longer.

2 · The water test

  1. Take a mouthful of water. Do not swallow it.
  2. Say "ah". Still do not swallow.
  3. What you just did to stop the water going down is tightening the pharynx. That is the position.
  4. Now spit the water out and say red, road, router from that same position, with the lips in a slight o.

No water to hand: start to yawn, then stop halfway and hold it.

3 · /w/ or /r/?

Some say the English /r/ resembles the /w/ of week-end, but is not the same sound. Here is how to feel the difference. Tap any word to hear it.

  1. Hand on your vocal cords. Hold a long wwwww, then a long rrrrr.
  2. There is more vibration on /r/ than on /w/. That is the difference, and you can feel it before you can hear it.

4 · How many R sounds?

Not how many letters. How many times you actually make the sound. Say the word out loud first.

5 · When the silent R comes back

A final r is silent, unless the next word begins with a vowel sound. Then it comes back, to join the two words together. It's called the linking /r/.

The car is old.  →  The car_is old.
The server crashed.  →  no r, because crashed starts with a consonant.
The server is down.  →  The server_is down. The r comes back.

So server on its own has no /r/ at all, and server is has one. Same word. The sound belongs to the join, not to the word.

Everything on this page is British English. American English is rhotic: every written r is pronounced, with the tongue curled back. Pick one accent and be consistent.
